name: Wind-driven Particle Advection
definition: A particle advection technique where volumetric particles (voxels) are displaced by a wind vector field stored in a 3D grid. The wind field is sampled based on the particle's normalized position within the volume bounds.
summary: Wind-driven Particle Advection displaces volumetric particles through a static 3D wind vector field to simulate local cloud movement, differing from global flow methods by using a localized, discrete grid-based wind field.
